notes:
Account snapshot: fintech payments processor, heavy compliance needs (EU data residency + SOC2), latency sensitive for auth flows (p95 < 120ms for realtime fraud checks). Initial interest: Dedicated pools or Private VPC to keep keys in KMS and avoid external egress. Timeline was accelerated after Q3 security push — they ran parallel POC vs AWS managed endpoints. 

Key convo highlights:
- 2024-10-14 call (FF id ff_20241014_8132): Security lead: 'We need managed endpoint with vendor SLAs and integrated IAM; we can't take on patching risk right now.'
- 2024-11-02 demo: Redwood Dedicated perf looked strong (8–10ms/token on TGI-style model in our lab), SE Daniel ran throughput sim for 500 TPS with batching.
- 2024-11-18 security review: asked for evidence of KMS key separation and audit log retention — provided security FAQ + drive link.
- Dec 2024: Procurement pushed for single-cloud standardization; infra director hired a contractor who recommended SageMaker-managed endpoints for auditability and vendor support contract.

Why we lost:
- Security + procurement favored hyperscaler native managed endpoints (AWS SageMaker/Bedrock) for perceived lower operational overhead and consolidated billing.
- No enduring internal champion after infra director left in Dec; champion moved to a different org.
- Budget shift: CFO enforced cloud consolidation directive for FY25, deprioritized third-party dedicated infra.

POC artifacts: perf reports, cost model vs SageMaker (shared 2024-12), replay of demo in Drive.

Re-engagement signals to watch: change in procurement policy, champion rehire, proof of meaningful cost delta at scale, or GDPR/data residency event that requires more control than hyperscaler managed.

Suggested follow-ups: archive deal, schedule check-in 6mo post-close, keep security and cost comparison templates current for similar accounts.
